title: A redirected Piercing leftover is offered to other replacement holders
summary: The designer: Piercing combat damage redirected into Oorblak is dealt to Oorblak up to its lethal damage and the leftover goes to the player, because 'replacement effects only apply once in an effect'; the register states the claim as 'not redirected again'. The pilot verifier measured that the engine stops only the SAME replacement from applying again: a second Oorblak or a Blightsea Polyp in the region takes the leftover, and only a holder with a higher entity id sees it (a lower-id Polyp consumes the whole hit first). The rule states the ruling (no further redirection).

evidence.quote: the other 6 still reach the player, and are not redirected again.
the leftover is not redirected a second time.

closed: not a bug: the owner ruled on 2026-10-16 that a Piercing leftover "is still considered combat damage, so it'd go to the second one" and adopted Caleb's chain (each replacement effect applies once); the engine's chain is the rule (CT-228 ruled correct; 469 shows it).

title: 239 'the owner ruling of 2026-08-18 (“Formation changes during combat […]”) STILL STANDS' asserts at the Swift window, before the normal sub-step runs
summary: 239-damage-triggers-after-combat.test.ts 'the owner ruling of 2026-08-18 (“Formation changes during combat […]”) STILL STANDS' claims the Swift-killed Sprite dealt nothing in the normal sub-step and that only the trigger queue waits. Its board is a split step (a Swift blocker against a normal attacker), so after pass/pass/answerElections it is paused at the Swift/normal window: the 'dealt NOTHING in the normal sub-step' assertion is taken before the normal sub-step runs, and in a split step the trigger queue resolves at that window rather than waiting until after combat (owner ruling of 2026-09-16, “A split damage step is several…”). The test does not assert its title.

title: Vroot ('when my column deals combat damage', not 'to a player') does not trigger when its column's damage is wholly redirected into Oorblak
summary: Possible divergence outside this record's claim. The engine lumps Vroot with the 'deals combat damage to a player' listeners, so a column whose hit is wholly redirected into Oorblak gives Vroot nothing. But Vroot's trigger has no 'to a player'; Oorblak's text has the damage 'dealt to me instead', and the owner (2026-10-16) said it is still combat damage. Read that way, the column did deal combat damage (to Oorblak) and Vroot should pay out that much. Worth an owner check.

evidence.quote: assert.ok(!fired(hit(58111 + 3 * i, column, 'whole', setup).evs, name), `${name}: the column dealt the player nothing`);
assert.equal(vrootGain(evs), 4, 'the column dealt 4 combat damage, to Oorblak');

closed: fixed on 2026-10-23 (owner "Any combat damage", asked what Vroot counts): Vroot, Flowstone Arcanite and Blightmound count the combat damage their column deals to blockers, to Oorblak and to the player, and the "to a player" family is unchanged (601).

title: The engine opens no window before the Sluggish strike of a column that gained Sluggish after the step began
summary: The rule (the designer, 2025-04-20) has a column that gains Sluggish in the window after the Swift sub-step strike in the Sluggish sub-step, with the before-Sluggish window opening first. The engine fixes the damage step's sub-steps once, when the step opens (damageSubs), so a Sluggish sub-step that was not scheduled then gets no window before the gained Sluggish strike, and triggers from normal damage wait until after combat.

evidence.quote: a column that gains {Sluggish} during the damage step strikes in the Sluggish sub-step with no priority window before it
